commenti.body: That's an interesting observation - I think it's why at the end Nora isn't sad that she didn't choose Hae Sung, she's just overwhelmed finally thinking about all the ways her life could have turned out. it's just as likely if she stayed and married him she still would be more progressive in her thinking and would have grown tired of his traditional mindset. I like to think that her marriage grows stronger in the future as they both are grateful for each other and keep talking about their relationship.

This is a great perspective and so well written. Perfectly captures so much of what you feel when you watch it. It saddens me that a few reactions to the movie I saw flying around were very pessimistic and negative. I found it to be so beautiful and sad in the best ways in dealing with the soberness of life.
I found Nora to exemplify a young woman not afraid to confront her emotions but also not be led astray by them at the same time. There was a curiosity there having to do with her own personal identity and growth as a human. This last few minutes stunned me and I found myself sobbing with Nora.

there's a moment when she starts talking with Hae Sung on skype where he asks if he could call her Seung Ah and she remarks that nobody calls her that anymore, not even her mother. when she emigrated, she became Nora. she speaks, reads, writes and thinks in another language. she exists in a world with different possibilities and different expectations. but meeting Hae Sung again, especially face to face, makes her recall that part of her that stopped being when she left Seoul.   


in-yun is like eight-thousand layers deep. so when Seung Ah comes alive in her again, because Hae Sung is by her side, it's like dealing with eight thousand layers of possibilities that could have been, might have been, would have been. and that's a lot.

​

i'm an immigrant, just like Nora. and i get that part of the experience. i've become a different person because the possibilities that were once in front of me totally changed. and dealing with the new possibilities in a new world, i haven't thought much at all about the person i left behind. when those thoughts come back, they are overwhelming.

the movie is kinda advertised as a love story but the love part is just that, a part of the whole. the relationship that she develops with Arthur comes partly as a situation of convenience - they move in together cuz it's convenient, they get married so her immigration status could be secure. with those circumstances, their relationship looks to have grown strong and secure. 

movies about romance foreground the love story over all else but this movie really deals with the romantic relationship the way it can happen in real life.

and the connection between Nora and Hae Sung is not a romantic one at all. not for her, and actually not for him, either.
